title: A program can ask decade which pane its next window goes in
body:
A window from a process decade did not start is placed by its client's environment, as decided in decade-1919e9. `launched_from` in `decade/src/server/compositor.rs` reads `/proc/<pid>/environ`: `DECADE_WORKSPACE` finds the workspace, and `DECADE_PANE` finds the pane to split beside. The program has no say in the pane. acre's neovim plugin starts `acre-gui --stdio` as a viewer, and it may want that window in a scratch pane rather than beside neovim.

## Proposal

A program that starts a child sets `DECADE_INTO=<pane name>` in the child's environment. `launched_from` reads `DECADE_INTO` first and puts the window in that pane, as a new tab when the pane already shows a window. A name no pane answers to falls back to placement by `DECADE_PANE`. A program that sets nothing keeps today's placement.

## Rejected

- A socket request, with a `decade-channel` call, that names the pane for the next window. decade would have to match the request to the window, by the pid that will own it or by a token. A pid races the window, which can open before the request arrives, and misses windows from the child's own children. The environment reaches every process under the child with no matching.
- Replacing the window already in the named pane. Adding a tab closes nothing.

## Cost

`docs/protocol.md` documents the new variable. Adding it breaks nothing, so it moves `decade`'s patch. `decade-channel` does not change. The neovim plugin's change is acre's.
